So, I have a gaming PC and a laptop, and I rarely use the gaming PC for any type of productivity. In response, here is what I have done.

  1. Choose the game you plan to play on the PC, are you going to play PC games or mainly emulators? If you plan to run emulators, emulationstation is a good one. If you only plan on playing a single game, create a shortcut to that (with any arguments if it's an emulator game) as this will be the fastest startup for your game.

  2. Disable your password, remember, this is NOT a productivity machine and does not need to be secure. On Windows 10, this will automatically enable auto sign-in, so no more is needed here.

  3. Open task scheduler, create a task, trigger should be set to "at log on" for specific user

  4. Under actions, it should be set to run a program, now copy-paste the shortcut to Big Picture, emulationstation, or whatever game you decided to start up right away. No need to separate the argument since Windows will do it for you.

  5. Uncheck all conditions under conditions tab, then uncheck everything under settings except for "Allow task to be run on demand"

  6. Hit OK, save the task, then reboot your computer.

Personally, I'm playing Zelda: Twilight Princess on Dolphin exclusively on that computer, so I set it so as soon as my computer boots up, the game pops up and it's ready to play immediately after the OS has started.
